sections.content:
The DOWN probe didn't move the player — only the HUD cell (63,63) changed from M→W. The cell below the player (rows 18-20, cols 15-17) is open black. So why didn't the player move?
Hypotheses:
1. The player moves 3 pixels (1 cell) per action, but the move was blocked... no, the cell below is open.
2. The player moves 1 pixel per action, but the move was blocked... the pixel below (18, 15-17) is open.
3. The arrow keys don't directly move the player. Maybe they rotate the player's facing direction, and the player moves automatically? Or the player is controlled by something else.
4. Maybe the player only moves when the key is pressed and the destination is open — but the destination is open.
Wait — maybe the player is a 3x3 sprite and moves in 3-pixel increments, and the move was blocked because... hmm, rows 18-20, cols 15-17 are open.
Let me reconsider: maybe the player is at cell (5,5) in a 3x3 cell grid, and the walls are 3x3 blocks. The cell below (6,5) is open. So DOWN should move the player 3 pixels down. But it didn't.
Maybe... the action is being consumed as a "step" but the player is stationary because the game is a "maze where you slide until you hit a wall"? Even so, it should move.
Or maybe the player only moves when the entire 3x3 destination region is open — and it is open.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the player's position is defined by the center pixel (16,16). Moving down 1 pixel: center (17,16) — that's within the player's own 3x3. If the game treats the player as 1x1 at the center and checks the destination pixel (17,16)... that's the player's own pixel, so maybe it's blocked by itself? Unlikely.
Or maybe the game checks the destination cell as the 3x3 block below: rows 18-20, cols 15-17 — open.
Let me look at the HUD: the M band on row 63. (63,63) changed from M to W. So the HUD bar is decreasing from the right side. This is probably a "remaining moves" bar. It advances with each action.
Actually, wait — maybe the player did move, but the frame I'm looking at is... no, the diff was only 1 cell.
Let me think about this game from a different angle. This might be a "push" game or a "laser" game... but the simplest is: maybe the arrow keys move the player 1 cell (3 pixels) per action, and the move was blocked because the game requires the destination cell to be open AND the player to not be in a "locked" state?
Or maybe the player is actually a 1x1 at the center (16,16), and the blue 3x3 is just a glow/sprite. Moving down 1 pixel from (16,16) to (17,16): (17,16) is 'b' — part of the sprite. If the game checks the destination pixel against the wall set (W, w, g, G), then 'b' is not a wall, so it should move.
Hmm, let me try another direction and see if any direction moves the player. Let me try RIGHT — to the right of the player is a 'g' wall at cols 18-20, rows 15-17. If RIGHT is blocked and UP works, that's informative.
Actually, let me try UP: rows 12-14, cols 15-17 are open. If UP moves the player, then movement works and DOWN is specifically blocked (maybe there's an invisible wall below? But the ascii shows B).
Wait, actually — maybe I should reconsider. The player moves 3 pixels per action, and the move was blocked because the game checks the destination cell as rows 18-20, cols 15-17... open. I keep going in circles.
Let me just probe UP and RIGHT (2 actions) and observe. No, to save actions, let me probe UP alone first. If the player moves up 3 pixels, then DOWN is blocked for some reason (maybe a one-way wall?). If UP doesn't move either, then the arrow keys don't move the player directly.
Hmm, wait. Another idea: maybe the player is stationary and the arrow keys move a "cursor" or "pointer" that I can't see... but the board didn't change at all (except the HUD). So the arrow keys had no visible effect on the board.
Or: maybe the game requires the player to be on a "path" and the player is currently... the player is at (15,15), which is at the edge of the maze. The maze walls start at rows 15-17. The player overlaps with the maze boundary region (rows 15-17, cols 15-17 is the top-left corner of the maze).
Let me look at the whole maze in cell units (3x3 cells). Let me downsample: for each 3x3 cell (i,j), check if it's a wall. The board is 64x64, not divisible by 3. The maze seems to span rows 15-47, cols 15-47 (33x33 = 11x11 cells). The player is at cell (0,0) of the maze, the target is at cell (10,10).
Let me build the 11x11 cell map and see the maze structure. Then I'll figure out the movement.
